# Generated failures and endpoint classes point back to the Phrase source
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #161, sha256:cd3ba2a587dea1ded0e0bfc758edcbc7c44a96c07b6381eb1ce48d95751ca6b9). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; from the Usable v1 retro product feedback)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product feedback gathered from Codex and Grok at the Usable v1 retro, 2026-10-28 (docs/retros/usable-v1-2026-10-28.md): the demo's real rules, validation, storing and updating, all sit in native C#, so a cold model has to learn generated C# conventions to change them and a reader of the Phrase cannot see the rule.
- **Depends on:** 138
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want any failure of a generated API to be traceable to its Phrase endpoint, step and spec through a source map and a trace command, so that I can find the spec without reading the generated C# and without the running API exposing source details.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work; amended by Decider D113, 2026-10-28):**
  1. Given the Tasks demo, When phrase build runs and the API is started and each declared failure (EmptyTitle, TitleTooLong, NotFound, StoreUnavailable) is triggered over real HTTP, Then the source map written by the build resolves each failure and every endpoint to the exact Phrase line and endpoint in demo/tasks/Tasks.phrase (expected lines computed from the source text, not hardcoded), and the map carries stable opaque step ids, a build id compiled into the assembly, and csHash values
  2. Given the shared no-Phrase-knowledge assertions (no file name with a line number, no // phrase: comment, no X-Phrase-Source, no map reference in the generated C#), When a generated string containing each forbidden pattern is fed to them, Then they throw, and the same assertions pass on the real generated output
  3. Given the generated C# for orders.phrase and the demo, When the card is merged, Then it is byte-identical to before this card except for the PhraseBuild.cs assembly metadata file (the recorded orders hash is unchanged), the 422 bodies and the 11 specs are unchanged, the README drift test and the Usable v1 bars stay green, and the same source gives the same map and C# on Windows and Linux and from another directory

**Partly verified until the split cards land (D113):** that the map is not in publish output and is not served (card 167), and the trace command's mismatch handling and error paths (card 168). Also split out: culture-independent order (169), independent step-id recompute and one id per failure per endpoint (170), CLI reads names from the adapter and a tidy Program.cs (171).

## Context

- A reader the personas may miss: the engineer on call who must trace a production failure back through generated code (found at the Usable v1 retro). Prefer the smallest change that makes the trace possible.

- Decision D111 (2026-10-28, supersedes D110): traceability is a source map outside the runtime, not knowledge inside the generated C#. The header, its switch and the // phrase: comments were reverted (commit 1b287f3). #line directives are a separate card.

- Decision D112 (2026-10-28): the failure observer is its own card (165). This card adds one requirement: the source map gives every endpoint, step and failure a stable opaque step id (a short hash of the normalised position and name, deterministic across platforms) that the observer later reuses.
